title: Find a customer on the Customers page

steps.expect: Title 'Customers' with a plain number beside it (e.g. '1,234', no word after it). Columns: Customer, Source, Pipeline, Created. Newest customers first. Footer reads 'Page 1 of N'.
steps.note: title=true count='772' cols=Customer|Source|Pipeline|Created footer='Previous Page 1 of 39 Next' newestFirst=true

steps.do: Type part of a customer's name, email or phone in 'Search by name, email or phone…'.
steps.expect: Rows narrow to matches; the number beside the title drops to the match count; the URL gains a pc… search key.
steps.note: search 'gmail' (email part): count 772→199; url /dashboard/customers?pc_q=gmail; all rows match=true

steps.do: Open Filters, pick Pipeline = Fresh, then a Created date range.
steps.expect: Chips for each filter appear under the bar; every row's Pipeline badge reads Fresh and its Created date sits in the range. While the new rows load, the old rows fade a little (only if it takes longer than a moment) and come back to full strength when the new ones land.
steps.note: chips=["Pipeline: Fresh","Created: Jan 1 → Nov 25","Pipeline: Fresh","Created: Jan 1 → Nov 25"]; preset 'Year to Date'; 20 rows all Fresh=true; createdAt param={"from":"2026-01-01T08:00:00.000Z","to":"2026-11-26T07:59:59.999Z"}; dates Aug 18, 2026..Oct 14, 2026; fade on pipeline change (1.5s delayed): stale=true minOpacity=0.60 end=1; on date change: stale=true min=0.60 end=1

steps.expect: The whole table is replaced by an empty state: 'No customers' / 'No customers match these filters'. No pagination footer, no grey placeholder rows.
steps.note: body='No customers No customers match these filters' table=0 footer=0 skeletons=0

steps.do: Clear the search and remove the chips.
steps.expect: All customers come back; the number returns to the full total.

steps.do: Click the Customer column header, then Created.
steps.expect: Rows re-sort by name, then by created date. Pipeline is not sortable.
steps.note: sort buttons {"Customer":2,"Source":1,"Pipeline":0,"Created":1}; after Customer: url /dashboard/customers?pc_sort=name&pc_dir=asc, names A→Z (, ,  Zuhier Damouni…); after Created: url /dashboard/customers?pc_dir=asc, dates oldest first

steps.do: Go to page 2 with the footer's next button, then press the browser Back button.
steps.expect: Page 2 shows different customers; Back returns to page 1 with the same filters.
steps.note: page2 url /dashboard/customers?pc_pipeline=fresh&pc_p=2 ('Previous Page 2 of 11 Next', different rows=true); Back → /dashboard/customers?pc_pipeline=fresh ('Previous Page 1 of 11 Next'), same rows as p1=true

steps.do: Hover a row and open its ⋯ menu next to the name.
steps.expect: Exactly three items: View Profile, Schedule Meeting, Delete. No 'Edit Profile'.
steps.note: menu: View Profile | Schedule Meeting | Delete

steps.do: Choose View Profile (or click the row anywhere else).
steps.expect: The customer's profile opens over the page; closing it leaves the table where it was.
steps.note: profile overlay opened=true ('Oli Test's Profile Map unavailable — check console for diagnostics Street Aerial Map OT Oli Test 6252 Calvin Avenue, Tar'), url while open /dashboard/customers?pc_pipeline=fresh; after Escape closed=true, url /dashboard/customers?pc_pipeline=fresh, table unchanged=true; row click opens profile=true

steps.expect: A date-and-time picker opens (super-admin only). Close it with Escape without picking anything.
steps.note: date trigger button=true; picker opened=true; closed by Escape without picking=true

steps.do: In the top search bar type a common first name that matches at least 5 customers, then pick 'See all matches in Customers'.
steps.expect: The Customers page opens with that name already in its search box and only matching rows.
steps.note: 'John' (16 matches) → /dashboard/customers?pc_q=John; search box='John'; rows all match=true (16)

why: 5e97899c8: the Customers page was rebuilt on the new useCustomersTable hook and EntityRecordsTable (DataView parts); the table's own empty row went (7e179f51e); Edit Profile removed (e1bb84e7c); search.service now reads CUSTOMERS_RECORDS_TABLE_VIEW.
